topicName: Understanding new features in recent Oracle versions (e.g., 19c, 21c, 23c)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding New Features in Recent Oracle Versions (19c, 21c, 23c)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides an overview of significant new features introduced in recent Oracle Database versions, specifically 19c, 21c, and 23c. Understanding these features can help you optimize database performance, enhance security, and leverage new development capabilities."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Oracle 19c: The Long-Term Support Release"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Oracle 19c is the terminal release of the 12c Release 2 code line and is designated as a long-term support release. It includes numerous enhancements and bug fixes accumulated over previous releases. Key features include:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Automatic Indexing: The database automatically creates and maintains indexes based on workload analysis, improving query performance without manual intervention."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Real-Time Statistics: Provides more accurate statistics for the optimizer, leading to better execution plans."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SQL Quarantine: Prevents poorly performing SQL statements from impacting the entire system by automatically quarantining them."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Online Datafile Move: Allows moving datafiles while the database is online, minimizing downtime."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"-- Example of checking if automatic indexing is enabled
SELECT parameter_value FROM dba_auto_index_config WHERE parameter_name = 'AUTO_INDEX_MODE';"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Oracle 21c: Innovation Release"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Oracle 21c is an innovation release, introducing cutting-edge features and technologies. Note that innovation releases typically have shorter support lifecycles compared to long-term support releases. Key features include:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Native JSON Datatype: Provides native support for JSON data, allowing for efficient storage and querying of JSON documents."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Blockchain Tables: Enables creating immutable tables for secure and transparent data management."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"AutoML: Automates the machine learning model building process, making it easier for developers to integrate machine learning into their applications."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JavaScript in the Database: Allows executing JavaScript code directly within the database, enabling new development paradigms."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"-- Example of creating a JSON column
ALTER TABLE employees ADD (employee_data JSON);"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Oracle 23c: The Next Generation Database"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Oracle 23c introduces significant enhancements across various areas, including developer productivity, data management, and security. Key features include:"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SQL Domains: Allows defining reusable data types and constraints, improving data quality and consistency."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JSON Relational Duality Views: Enables accessing JSON data as relational tables and vice versa, simplifying data integration."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"True Cache: A client-side, in-memory cache that significantly improves application performance by reducing database round trips."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"JavaScript Stored Procedures: Enhances JavaScript integration by allowing the creation of stored procedures written in JavaScript."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"-- Example of creating a SQL Domain
CREATE DOMAIN email_address AS VARCHAR2(255)
CHECK (REGEXP_LIKE(VALUE, '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,4}'));"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Oracle 19c, 21c, and 23c offer a range of new features and enhancements that can significantly improve database performance, security, and development efficiency. Choosing the right version depends on your specific requirements and the desired level of support. Always review the official Oracle documentation for detailed information and best practices."}]
